facts.content: Patient reports a 'blinding' headache for 3 days.
The headache had a sudden onset upon waking and is constant.
Pain is 8/10 intensity, reduced to 5/10 with ibuprofen but never fully resolves.
Headache is diffuse and increases over the right eye, worsens with standing quickly or head movement.
facts.source_text: Diffuse, ↑ over R eye; ↑ when standing quickly/head movement

facts.content: There is photophobia and intermittent flashing lights or visual disturbance.
Patient experiences mild nausea without vomiting.
No focal neurological symptoms, fever, or upper respiratory tract infection/sinus symptoms.
facts.source_text: No focal neuro Sx, no fever, no URTI/sinus Sx

facts.content: Patient sleeps through the night but wakes with a headache.
facts.source_text: Sleeps through night but wakes w/ H/A;

facts.content: Concentration is impaired and patient missed 1.5 days of work.
Patient has only tried ibuprofen for relief.
Patient has no significant past medical history.
Mother has migraines.
Patient uses oral contraceptive pills started 1 year ago.
Patient takes ibuprofen as needed.
Patient has no known allergies.
Patient lives alone, does not smoke, and consumes about 3 alcoholic drinks per week.
Patient does not use illicit drugs and has no recent travel.
facts.source_text: no illicit drugs; no recent travel

facts.content: Assessment is a new severe headache with photophobia and visual aura, possibly a migraine or secondary cause.
facts.source_text: New severe H/A w/ photophobia & visual aura—?migraine vs secondary cause

facts.content: Review need for oral contraceptive pill use if migraine with aura is confirmed.

facts.content: Pain control is suboptimal.
There is a limitation of work and activities of daily living.
Schedule an in-person visit for a full neurological exam, fundoscopy, and blood pressure check.
facts.source_text: Book in-person visit: full neuro exam, fundoscopy, BP check

facts.content: Prescribe a stronger NSAID and paracetamol, instruct to take with food and avoid excess ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: Rx stronger NSAID + paracetamol; take w/ food; avoid excess ibuprofen

facts.content: Educate patient on red flags and advise to attend A&E if worsening, neuro deficit, altered pattern, or intolerable pain.

facts.content: Reassess the use of OCP and switch if migraine with aura is confirmed.
